You'll take an idea from a rough direction to working software in production, mostly on your own. This is a hands-on role: you'll write a lot of code, and you'll orchestrate a lot of agents to write more of it. Who is Digistore24? Digistore24 is the all-in-one online sales platform that combines the world's largest international affiliate marketplace with industry-leading conversion tools. Founded in Germany in 2012, we've been the online market leader in Germany since 2014 and have been expanding rapidly in the US since 2020. Today, more than 5 million users and 125,000+ active affiliates work with us, and over $5.1 billion in sales has gone through the platform. We're self-funded and work fully remote, with team members across Europe and the US. Eklektika, a company from Belgrade, has existed for 20 years and recently became an integral part of the German/USA company Digistore24. What you'll be working on Digistore24 is one of the world's leading online sales platforms, with the largest international affiliate marketplace in the industry. Vendors use us to sell, affiliates use us to find offers to promote, and more than 5 million users work with us. You'll work on what comes next: new products and new capabilities on the platform, with a strong focus on AI and how agents will change commerce. Most of the work is new. You'll build new services and products rather than maintain old ones, though you'll sometimes dig through our existing PHP codebase to work out how things behave today and what a new version needs to do. The scope will change, and a lot of it will start as a prototype. You'll start with a few specific workflows. Within roughly your first four months, the goal is to have something real shipped and in the hands of pilot customers. What you'll do Turn direction into working software. Take a goal from the CTO, break it down, plan your own work, decide how to build it, and ship it. Escalate only when something really needs it. Build end-to-end, backend first. Services, APIs, data pipelines, and integrations, plus the frontend on top. Whatever the problem needs. Mine the old to build the new. Read the existing codebase to pull out the real requirements, edge cases, and business rules a new version has to respect. Prototype, then harden. Get something working fast, learn from it, and turn what works into production-quality software. Run what you build. Deployment, monitoring, and cost control are part of the job. You know where agents can be trusted and where a human has to stay in the loop, especially around money. You're tool-agnostic.
